newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban says key town taken from foes.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban says key town taken from foes.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic militia said it had retaken the strategic town of Jabal os-Siraj north of the capital Kabul hours after it fell to their opponents.

A Taleban spokesman, quoted by the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) news service, said the opposition assault on the town had been repulsed and "now Jabal os-Siraj is fully under our control".

AIP had earlier reported that opposition forces led by renowned guerrilla commander Ahmad Shah Masood had also taken Golbahar town at the mouth of his native Pansher Valley, and were fighting south of Jabal os-Siraj to take the Parwan province capital of Charikar.
The Taleban spokesman said thousands more fighters had been sent to the frontline to reinforce the militia against opposition attacks.
